body:
Follow-up to #2962. This replaces the memo version of this branch, on @lballabio's point that the lookup is not needed at all.

`DiscretizedCallableFixedRateBond::preAdjustValuesImpl()` and `postAdjustValuesImpl()` run at every step of the rollback over every coupon and every callability, and each test went through `isOnTime()` — `close_enough(grid[grid.index(t)], time())`. The lookup is not computing a grid time: `TimeGrid::index(t)` throws unless `t` belongs to the grid, and when it returns `i`, `grid[i]` is `t` within tolerance. It is a validator, and the comparison does not need it.

## Change

`isOnTime(t)` becomes `close_enough(t, time())` at the three call sites. The cache, the two arrays, the NaN sentinels, the lattice pointer and the grid-identity check are gone.

The validation the lookup also performed is kept where it can fail: the `TimeGrid` constructor overload takes the caller's grid unchanged, so `calculateWithSpread()` checks — once per valuation, and only for that path — that every event time is a grid node and that no second node matches it. Grids the engine builds from `mandatoryTimes()` contain the event times by construction and are not re-checked.

## Measurements

Callable bond OAS benchmark: 30-year semiannual bond, monthly calls at par, Black-Karasinski, 100 steps. Each timing is one OAS solve plus three `cleanPriceOAS` calls, median of three runs, on a 2 vCPU machine.

| Case | `master` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| 30y monthly calls, a=1e-4 | 1472 ms | 1400 ms |
| 30y monthly calls, a=0.03 | 1405 ms | 1361 ms |

At these timings the run-to-run spread on this machine is on the order of ±10%, so read the wall clock as "not slower"; the binary search the memo cached is now absent from the per-step path rather than remembered.

All twelve configurations of the benchmark harness print bit-identical `oas`, `cleanAtOas`, `cleanUp`, `cleanDown` and `oasd` against `master` (the `bits=` field is equal on every line).

## Tests

`testCallerSuppliedGridMustContainEventTimes` in `test-suite/callablebonds.cpp`:

* a caller-supplied grid holding the bond's event times reproduces the price of the engine-built grid;
* a caller-supplied grid holding only the endpoints throws instead of silently pricing without the coupons and calls it does not contain.

comments.body: Thanks.  I was also thinking about the `T = grid[grid.index(t)]; return close_enough(T, time())` pattern that we're using, cached or not.  We seems to be doing this in order to check (via `grid.index`) that `t` is, in fact, on the grid.  But didn't we adjust the coupon times etc to the grid already?  Couldn't we just say `close_enough(t, time())`?

Thanks for reviewing, @lballabio . This PR was obviously LLM-generated, based on a backport of https://github.com/amaggiulli/QLNet/pull/331 . I, the human, looked at it now. Your comments are valid and it looks like it will lead to an even better performance improvement. I'll submit a new PR for this. Thanks for your gracious response, as always. The flood of AI-generated PRs surely is challenging.

@lballabio you were right — the lookup only checks that `t` is on the grid, and the grid the engine builds already contains every coupon and call date. I rewrote this branch rather than opening another PR:

* `isOnTime(t)` is now `close_enough(t, time())` at the three call sites; the memo, the two arrays, the NaN sentinels and the invalidation rule are gone.
* The check is kept only where it can fail. The `TimeGrid` constructor overload uses the caller's grid unchanged, so that path now validates it once per valuation: every event time must be a node, and no second node may match it. Grids built from `mandatoryTimes()` are not re-checked.
* New test covers both: a supplied complete grid reproduces the engine price, a grid with only the endpoints throws.

Measured on the 30y monthly-call cases: 1472 → 1400 ms and 1405 → 1361 ms; all twelve benchmark configurations bit-identical to `master`.

title: Compare callable-bond event times directly instead of looking them up
